_source: Rise Fall Repeat Short, watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-19: frames at 0/0.5/1/1.5/2/2.5/3 s then every 3 s to the end plus the last frame (shot edges to about 1.5 s), word timings from YouTube's caption track. Our own descriptions. 313K views. YouTube marks it 'AI': generated 1930s stills, slow push; the last second is a six-panel collage of the product in everyday use. Not probed for sound (same channel and mix as vBw4jNaJQ28).

hook.firstFrame: a thin young man in a worn 1930s suit standing in a muddy workshop yard, cold blue-grey light; caption with a year
hook.firstLine: in the 1930s a twenty-year-old had nothing left

shots.picture: young man in a worn suit standing alone in a muddy workshop yard
the same man slumped on a crate among scrap, pedestrians passing
a boss handing him a box of rusty parts over a counter
close on hands pressing metal teeth onto tape at a cramped bench
the man exhausted at the bench by a window, piles of jammed zippers
a crowded period street, nobody looking at his stall
the man holding up a shiny imported zipper, then his face falling
head in hands at a desk, then new machines arriving in the workshop
thread knotted in a jammed machine, the man pulling at it
suppliers laughing in a doorway; the man standing firm
molten brass glowing orange in a furnace, the man working it
a busy factory floor, workers at machines under hand-lettered banners
a modern glass headquarters tower, low angle
extreme close-up of a jeans zipper pull with the maker's letters
six-panel collage: zippers on a bag, a jacket, a smiling woman, an old man

lines.gist: a twenty-year-old founder-to-be is introduced, completely broke
his employer went bust and paid him in a box of zipper parts
he made zippers by hand in a cold room; they jammed and nobody bought
a cheaper, stronger import made his product look hopeless
he spent his savings on machines, then bad thread jammed them
suppliers refused to help, so he decided to make everything himself
he made his own metal, thread and machines and a do-good motto
that box became a firm making half the world's zippers: check your clothes

ending.cta: look at the zipper on your own clothes
ending.lastFrame: a collage of zippers on everyday clothes and bags

whyItWorks: The underdog's misery is stacked for 90 seconds before the company's size is revealed.
The ending turns the story onto an object the viewer is wearing right now.
The company is in the title, so the story can open on the poor founder and still feel promised.
One protagonist in every still, ageing and changing setting, gives a single visual thread.
